title: Angle relationships
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.geo.angles.pairs: A right angle is 90°, a straight line 180°. Vertical angles (opposite where lines cross) are equal.
hints.geo.angles.triangle: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°.
hints.geo.angles.parallel: Parallel lines and a transversal make only two sizes of angle: the small ones are equal, the big ones are equal, and small + big = 180°.
hints.geo.angles: Right angle 90°, straight line 180°, triangle 180°, vertical angles equal.

misconceptionMessages.geo.comp-supp-swap: Complementary angles add to 90° (a right angle); supplementary angles add to 180° (a straight line).
misconceptionMessages.geo.vertical-supplementary: Vertical angles (opposite each other) are equal, not adding to 180°.
misconceptionMessages.geo.triangle-360: A triangle's angles add to 180°, not 360°.
misconceptionMessages.geo.isosceles-not-halved: There are two equal angles sharing what's left: halve it.
misconceptionMessages.geo.parallel-equal-supp: Is one angle small and the other big? Then they add to 180°. Both the same size? Then they're equal.

sections.title: Angle pairs
sections.objective: Use complementary, supplementary and vertical angles.
explain: Angles that make a right angle together are complementary (90°). Angles that make a straight line are supplementary (180°).
Where two lines cross, the opposite angles are vertical angles: they're equal.

steps: The two angles make a straight line, so they add to 180°.

sections.key: Right angle: add to 90°. Straight line: add to 180°. Vertical angles: equal.

sections.title: Angles in a triangle
sections.objective: Find a missing angle in a triangle.
explain: Tear the three corners off any triangle and they fit together on a straight line: 180°.
sections.key: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. Subtract the ones you know.

sections.title: Parallel lines
sections.objective: Find angles where a line crosses two parallel lines.
explain: A line crossing two parallel lines (a transversal) makes the same angles at both crossings.
There are only two sizes: small and big, and small + big = 180°.

steps: Angles 2 and 6 are in the same spot at each crossing (corresponding angles).
They're both small angles, so they're equal.

sections.key: Same size (both small or both big): equal. One small and one big: they add to 180°.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: 90° for a right angle, 180° for a straight line and for a triangle. Vertical angles are equal.
